doc.title: Frank Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 7, 1998

chapter: Freelance years and The Loud Minority
title: Freelance starving
summary: He calls the 22 years before leading Basie his freelance starving, with no taste for promotion.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: I call it freelance starving. People tell me like the 22 years that I was out of the Basie Orchestra until I took over as leader, that was my period of freelance starving.
Gee when you left Basie you were in your late 30s?
Yes. I was in my mid-30s.
So it was almost like a — you know you think of athletes retiring from a certain type of thing that they’ve done for so long and now it’s on to something else.
I didn’t have the mentality to go into promotion or —
Well I’m glad you stayed with music.
